title: Finite-field cohomological dimension for all torsion sheaves
statement: Let $K$ be a finite field. For every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$, ordinary derived global-section cohomology vanishes in every degree $q>1$. Thus its all-torsion cohomological dimension [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] is at most one; no common annihilator or fixed prime is assumed.

proof.text: For a torsion sheaf M, finite-stalk subobjects have supremum top by lem-sc-field-torsion-finite-stalk-subobjects-cover. The bottom subobject has zero stalk. A binary supremum is the image of the biproduct, whose stalk is a finite product, so finite-stalk subobjects form a nonempty directed poset. Shrink it to Type(u+1). The Grothendieck abelian subobject-supremum colimit criterion gives a filtered colimit cocone with vertex M. Its members remain torsion: section maps of each subobject injection are injective, so the local annihilators in M also kill the lifted sections.

Decompose each finite-stalk torsion sheaf into a finite family of primary sheaves, with projection-inclusion composites summing to the identity, by lem-sc-generic-finite-primary-decomposition. This applies to any field, without a curve hypothesis.

For a finite primary stalk, the finite p-group exponent theorem supplies a power of the prime annihilating every stalk element. Additivity of the stalk functor turns this into equality of the images of that power times the sheaf identity and zero. The covering geometric point family is jointly faithful, so this same power annihilates the sheaf. This is the faithful-stalk consequence of the field stalk equivalence. An object annihilated by a fixed prime power is prime-power torsion in the kernel-colimit convention: lift its identity to the kernel at that exponent, then to the colimit. The composite back is the identity. On each kernel injection the other composite is the identity after passing to the sum of the two exponents; colimit hom-ext proves the equality.

The finite-field clause of sk-lem-base-field-cd bounds prime-power cohomological dimension by one. Rewrite it using det-cd-etale-comparison. A nonzero cohomology group of the primary sheaf in a degree q>1 would put q in the set whose supremum is at most one, a contradiction. For the finite-stalk sheaf, apply the additive cohomology functor to the finite sum of projection-inclusion composites. Each term factors through a zero cohomology object, so the image identity is zero. Additivity is transported from Sheaf.H using lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison.

Apply large filtered-colimit continuity of derived etale cohomology on the affine field spectrum to the cocone of step 1. Each member has zero cohomology above one by steps 2--4, so the colimit vertex does too. This proves the all-torsion bound without a common annihilator. The bottom subobject and empty primary family include the zero sheaf.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1--3: finite-stalk approximation and primary decomposition followed by the existing base-field prime-power bound; complete Lean assembly by U5, 2026-10-19
